context: The horizontal axis is input size n, marked from 1 to 14. The vertical axis is operation count T(n), with no numerical tick labels. The curves illustrate growth trends. They do not give measured counts for a particular program or unscaled function values.
description: The table orders the curves from lowest to highest at their right ends, following the upward arrow labeled “Lower to higher, better to worse.”

frames.explanation: Some curves cross early on. For example, the red exponential curve starts below the blue linear and orange quadratic curves, then overtakes them. The crossings are illustrative. They do not specify exact operation counts or the input size at which one algorithm becomes more efficient than another. For sufficiently large n, a lower order means slower growth in the operation count.
frames.title: Growth rates of five common time complexities

summary: The chart compares how five time complexities grow with input size.

tables.caption: Five time complexities and their curve shapes
headers: Complexity (lowest to highest at the right edge)
rows: A green horizontal line. The operation count stays the same as n changes.
A cyan curve rises slowly, with a gradually decreasing slope.
A straight blue line rises at a constant slope.
An orange curve bends upward and gets steeper.
A red curve stays near the bottom at first, then rises steeply.

title: Growth rates of five common time complexities
